chapters.title: Chapter 1 · The Ascension; Matthias Chosen
chapters.intro: This book picks up where the Gospel of Luke ends. For forty days after rising, Jesus appears to the apostles, tells them to stay in Jerusalem until the Holy Spirit comes, and is then taken up into heaven before their eyes. They go back to the city and pray together with the others. Peter proposes filling the place Judas left, and by casting lots Matthias is chosen. Verses 18–19 are an aside by the narrator.

verses.en: The first account I made, O Theophilus, about all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,

cmp.note: 「前一卷书」指《路加福音》：两卷书都是写给提阿非罗的，一般认为出自同一个作者，这一卷接着那一卷往下讲。
cmp.en: The "first account" is the Gospel of Luke: both books are addressed to Theophilus, are generally held to be by the same author, and this one takes up where that one ends.

verses.en: until the day when he was taken up, after giving commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen;
to whom he also presented himself alive after his suffering by many proofs, appearing to them over forty days and speaking of the things concerning the kingdom of God.
And while eating with them, he commanded them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father, “which you heard from me;

cmp.note: 这个词意思不很确定：可以是「一同吃饭」（字面是一同吃盐），也可以是「聚在一起」。白话取前一种，和合本取后一种。原文从这一节的后半句起，由转述变成直接引耶稣的话。
cmp.en: The meaning of this word is uncertain: either "eating with" (literally, sharing salt) or "being gathered with." This site takes the first, the Union Version the second. From the second half of the verse the Greek slips from reported speech into Jesus’s own words.

verses.en: for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”
So when they had come together, they were asking him, saying, “Lord, is it at this time that you are restoring the kingdom to Israel?”
And he said to them, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority,
but you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and to the end of the earth.”
And having said these things, while they were looking on, he was lifted up, and a cloud took him out of their sight.
And as they were gazing into heaven while he was going, look, two men in white clothing stood by them,
who also said, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him going into heaven.”
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

And when they had entered, they went up to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas the son of James.
All these were devoting themselves with one accord to prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
And in those days Peter stood up among the brothers—the crowd of persons gathered together was about a hundred and twenty—and said,
“Men, brothers, the scripture had to be fulfilled which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus,
for he was numbered among us and received his share in this ministry.”
Now this man acquired a field with the wages of his wrongdoing, and falling headlong he burst open in the middle, and all his bowels gushed out.

cmp.note: 第 18、19 两节，底本用破折号标成插在彼得讲话中间的一段说明，一般认为是叙述者替读者补的交代。本站照这样处理，所以引号在第 17 节收、第 20 节重开。犹大的结局，《马太福音》27:3–8 的说法和这里不同，两处各照原文译。
cmp.en: The edition sets verses 18–19 off with dashes as an aside inside Peter’s speech; they are generally taken as the narrator’s explanation for the reader. This site follows that, closing the quotation at verse 17 and reopening it at verse 20. Matthew 27:3–8 tells the end of Judas differently; each passage is translated as it stands.

verses.en: And it became known to all who live in Jerusalem, so that the field was called in their own language Hakeldamach, that is, Field of Blood.
“For it is written in the book of Psalms: ‘Let his homestead become desolate, and let there be no one dwelling in it,’ and: ‘Let another take his office.’

cmp.note: 两句分别引自旧约《诗篇》69:25 和 109:8。
cmp.en: The two lines are from Psalm 69:25 and Psalm 109:8.

verses.en: So, of the men who have accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
beginning from the baptism of John until the day when he was taken up from us—one of these must become a witness with us of his resurrection.”
And they put forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus, and Matthias.
And they prayed and said, “You, Lord, who know the hearts of all, show which one of these two you have chosen
to take the place in this ministry and apostleship from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place.”
And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · Pentecost; Peter’s Speech
chapters.intro: On the day of Pentecost the Holy Spirit comes on those gathered together and they begin speaking in many languages; Jews in Jerusalem from every land each hear their own. Peter stands and gives a long speech (verses 14–36): this is what the prophet Joel foretold, and Jesus, who was put to death, God has raised and made both Lord and Christ. About three thousand are baptized that day, and the believers hold everything in common.

verses.en: And when the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all together in one place.
And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like the rushing of a violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
And there appeared to them tongues as of fire, being distributed, and one rested on each of them.
And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit was giving them to utter.

cmp.note: 原文的「舌头」和「语言」是同一个词（glōssa）：上一节是火一样的「舌头」，这一节是别种「语言」。和合本译「别国的话」。
cmp.en: In Greek "tongue" and "language" are one word (glōssa): tongues as of fire in the previous verse, other languages in this one. The Union Version has 别国的话 (bié guó de huà, "the speech of other countries").

verses.en: Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men from every nation under heaven.
And when this sound occurred, the multitude came together and was bewildered, because each one was hearing them speak in his own language.
And they were amazed and marveled, saying, “Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
And how is it that we hear, each of us in our own native language?
Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those who dwell in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,

cmp.note: 第 9–11 节数的这些民族和地方，大致从东边的波斯一带起，经过今天的伊拉克、土耳其，到南边的埃及、北非，再到西边的罗马，就是当时犹太人散居的各地。人名地名的写法照和合本。
cmp.en: The peoples and places listed in verses 9–11 run roughly from the Persian east through what is now Iraq and Turkey, south to Egypt and North Africa, and west to Rome: the lands where Jews then lived scattered. The Chinese spellings follow the Union Version.

verses.en: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, and visitors from Rome,
both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them telling in our own tongues the mighty works of God.”
And they were all amazed and perplexed, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”
But others, mocking, were saying, “They are filled with sweet wine.”
But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and addressed them: “Men of Judea and all who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.
For these men are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day;
but this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:

cmp.en: Verses 17–21 quote Joel 2:28–32.

verses.en: ‘And it shall be in the last days, God says, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams;
yes, on my male slaves and on my female slaves in those days I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.
And I will give wonders in the heaven above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke;
the sun shall be turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
And it shall be that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.’
Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested to you by God with mighty works and wonders and signs that God did through him in your midst, as you yourselves know—
this man, delivered up by the definite plan and foreknowledge of God, you nailed up by the hand of lawless men and killed.
But God raised him up, having loosed the pangs of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.
For David says concerning him: ‘I saw the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand so that I may not be shaken;

cmp.note: 第 25–28 节引自旧约《诗篇》16:8–11，照的是当时通行的希腊文译本。
cmp.en: Verses 25–28 quote Psalm 16:8–11, following the Greek version then in common use.

verses.en: therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced; moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope,
because you will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will you let your Holy One see decay.
You have made known to me the paths of life; you will fill me with gladness with your presence.’
Men, brothers, I may say to you with confidence about the patriarch David that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.
Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat one from the fruit of his loins on his throne,
he foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ, that he was neither abandoned to Hades nor did his flesh see decay.
This Jesus God raised up, of which we all are witnesses.
Being therefore exalted at the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he poured out this which you see and hear.
For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says: ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,

cmp.w: Eipen ho kyrios tōi kyriōi mou
cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》110:1。
cmp.en: A quotation of Psalm 110:1.

verses.en: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’
Let all the house of Israel therefore know for certain that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”
Now when they heard this they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “What shall we do, men, brothers?”
And Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit;
for the promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God calls to himself.”
And with many other words he testified solemnly and kept urging them, saying, “Be saved from this crooked generation.”
So those who received his word were baptized, and there were added that day about three thousand souls.
And they were devoting themselves to the teaching of the apostles and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.
And awe came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles.
And all who believed were together and had all things in common,
and they were selling their possessions and belongings and distributing them to all, as anyone had need.
And day by day, attending the temple together with one accord and breaking bread from house to house, they were sharing their food with glad and simple hearts,
praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord was adding to their number day by day those who were being saved.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · A Lame Man Healed; Peter Speaks in Solomon’s Portico
chapters.intro: Peter and John go up to the temple to pray and at its gate heal, in the name of Jesus, a beggar lame from birth. The people run to see, and Peter addresses them (verses 12–26): it is not we who healed this man but Jesus, whom you handed over and killed and whom God raised; repent, for the prophets spoke of these days long ago.

verses.en: Now Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
And a man lame from his mother’s womb was being carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms of those entering the temple;
who, seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple, asked to receive alms.
And Peter, gazing at him, together with John, said, “Look at us.”
And he fixed his attention on them, expecting to receive something from them.
But Peter said, “Silver and gold I do not have, but what I have, this I give you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, walk.”
And taking him by the right hand, he raised him up; and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong,
and leaping up, he stood and began to walk, and entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
And all the people saw him walking and praising God,
and they recognized him as the one who used to sit asking alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
And while he was clinging to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the portico called Solomon’s, utterly astonished.
And when Peter saw it, he answered the people: “Men of Israel, why do you marvel at this, or why do you gaze at us, as though by our own power or godliness we had made him walk?
The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his servant Jesus, whom you delivered up and denied before Pilate, when he had decided to release him.

cmp.note: 原文 pais 可以是「仆人」，也可以是「孩子、儿子」；这里多半是借用旧约《以赛亚书》里「上帝的仆人」的说法。和合本译「仆人」，并在 4:30 加小注「仆或作子」。
cmp.en: Greek pais can mean "servant" or "child, son"; here it most likely echoes the "servant of God" in Isaiah. The Union Version has 仆人 (púrén, "servant"), with a note at 4:30 that it may also be read "son."

verses.en: But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be granted to you,
and you killed the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.
And on the basis of faith in his name, his name has made strong this man whom you see and know; and the faith that is through him has given him this complete soundness in the presence of you all.
And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did also your rulers.
But what God announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ would suffer, he fulfilled in this way.
Repent therefore and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped out,
so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that he may send the Christ appointed for you, Jesus,
whom heaven must receive until the times of the restoration of all things, of which God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old.
Moses said: ‘The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers; you shall listen to him in everything that he says to you.

cmp.en: Verses 22–23 quote Deuteronomy 18:15–19 (with Leviticus 23:29).

verses.en: And it shall be that every soul that does not listen to that prophet shall be utterly destroyed from among the people.’
And all the prophets too, from Samuel and those who came after, as many as spoke, also announced these days.
You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with your fathers, saying to Abraham: ‘And in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed.’

cmp.en: A quotation of Genesis 22:18 (compare 12:3).

verses.en: To you first God, having raised up his servant, sent him to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4 · Peter and John before the Council; the Believers Pray
chapters.intro: The priests and Sadducees arrest Peter and John, and the next day the council questions them. Peter says the man was healed by the name of Jesus, and that there is salvation in no one else. Finding no ground to punish them, the council threatens them not to speak in that name again and lets them go. Back among their own, all pray together for boldness to speak. The chapter ends with the believers sharing everything, and Barnabas selling a field and giving the money.

verses.en: And as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
And they laid hands on them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about five thousand.
And it happened on the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem
—with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander and all who were of the high-priestly family—
and having set them in the midst, they were inquiring, “By what power or by what name did you do this?”
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders,
if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, by what means this man has been healed,

let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by him this man stands before you in good health.
This is ‘the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.’

cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》118:22；「你们」是彼得引的时候加进去的。
cmp.en: A quotation of Psalm 118:22; "by you" is added by Peter as he quotes it.

verses.en: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among people by which we must be saved.”
Now seeing the boldness of Peter and John, and perceiving that they were unlettered and ordinary men, they were marveling, and they recognized that they had been with Jesus.
And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.
But having ordered them to go outside the council, they were conferring with one another,
saying, “What shall we do with these men? For that a notable sign has been done through them is evident to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
But so that it may spread no further among the people, let us warn them to speak no more to anyone in this name.”
And having called them, they commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered and said to them, “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge;
for we cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard.”
And when they had threatened them further, they released them, finding no way to punish them, because of the people, for all were glorifying God for what had happened;
for the man on whom this sign of healing had been done was more than forty years old.
And when they were released, they went to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.
And when they heard it, they lifted their voice to God with one accord and said, “Sovereign Master, you who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them,
who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our father David your servant, said: ‘Why did the nations rage, and the peoples plot vain things?

cmp.note: 第 25–26 节引自旧约《诗篇》2:1–2。这一节开头那半句的希腊文很拗，各抄本写法不一，意思大致如此。
cmp.en: Verses 25–26 quote Psalm 2:1–2. The Greek of the opening clause is awkward and the manuscripts vary; the general sense is as given.

verses.en: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers were gathered together, against the Lord and against his Anointed.’

cmp.note: 「受膏者」原文就是 christos（基督）：这里照诗篇原来的意思译「受膏者」，下一节说上帝「膏立」了耶稣，用的是同一个词根。
cmp.en: "Anointed" is Greek christos, the word rendered "Christ" elsewhere; the next verse says God "anointed" Jesus, using the same root.

verses.en: For truly in this city there were gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the nations and the peoples of Israel,
to do whatever your hand and your plan had predestined to take place.
And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to your slaves to speak your word with all boldness,
while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are done through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”
And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and were speaking the word of God with boldness.
Now the multitude of those who believed were of one heart and soul, and not one said that any of his possessions was his own, but they had all things in common.
And with great power the apostles were giving their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
For there was not a needy person among them, for as many as were owners of lands or houses were selling them and bringing the proceeds of what was sold
and laying them at the feet of the apostles, and it was distributed to each as anyone had need.
And Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles—which translated means son of encouragement—a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
having a field, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the feet of the apostles.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 · Ananias and Sapphira; the Apostles Tried Again
chapters.intro: Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell a property, keep back part of the money and pretend to have handed over all of it; Peter says they have lied to God, and each in turn falls down dead. The apostles do many signs and are jailed by the high priest; an angel lets them out at night and they go back to teaching in the temple. The council tries them again, Gamaliel advises leaving them alone, and they are beaten and released.

verses.en: But a man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a piece of property,
and kept back some of the proceeds for himself, his wife also being aware of it, and bringing a certain part, he laid it at the feet of the apostles.
But Peter said, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back some of the proceeds of the land?
While it remained, did it not remain yours? And when it was sold, was it not under your authority? Why is it that you set this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God.”
And Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last; and great fear came upon all who heard.
And the young men rose and wrapped him up, and carrying him out they buried him.
Now there was an interval of about three hours, and his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
And Peter addressed her, “Tell me whether you sold the land for so much.” And she said, “Yes, for so much.”
But Peter said to her, “Why is it that you agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”
And immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last; and the young men, coming in, found her dead, and carrying her out they buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.

cmp.note: 「教会」这个词在这卷书里第一次出现。原文 ekklēsia 本来是「被召集起来的会众」，这里指信耶稣的这群人，不是指一座建筑。
cmp.en: This is the first time the word "church" appears in this book. Greek ekklēsia is properly "an assembly called together"; here it means the body of those who believe in Jesus, not a building.

verses.en: Now through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were being done among the people; and they were all with one accord in Solomon’s Portico.
But none of the rest dared to join them, yet the people held them in high esteem;
and all the more believers in the Lord were being added, multitudes of both men and women,
so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that as Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on some of them.
And the multitude from the towns around Jerusalem also was coming together, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and they were all being healed.
But the high priest rose up, and all who were with him, that is, the party of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy,
and they laid hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison.
But an angel of the Lord during the night opened the doors of the prison and, leading them out, said,
“Go, and standing in the temple speak to the people all the words of this life.”

And having heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began to teach. Now when the high priest came, and those who were with him, they called together the council and the whole senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.
But when the officers came, they did not find them in the prison, and they returned and reported,
saying, “We found the prison locked with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them we found no one inside.”
Now when the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed about them, wondering what this would come to.
And someone came and reported to them, “Look, the men whom you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.”
Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not with violence, for they were afraid of the people, lest they be stoned.
And having brought them, they set them in the council. And the high priest questioned them,
saying, “We strictly commanded you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.”
But Peter and the apostles answered and said, “We must obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.

cmp.note: 「挂在木头上」指钉十字架；这个说法出自旧约《申命记》21:22–23，那里说被挂在木头上的人是受咒诅的。
cmp.en: "Hanging on a tree" (literally "on wood") means crucifixion; the phrase comes from Deuteronomy 21:22–23, which says that one hanged on a tree is under a curse.

verses.en: God exalted him at his right hand as Leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.”
But when they heard this, they were enraged and wanted to kill them.
But a Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, stood up and gave orders to put the men outside for a little while,
and he said to them, “Men of Israel, take care what you are about to do with these men.
For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him; he was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.
After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew away people after him; he too perished, and all who followed him were scattered.
And now I tell you, keep away from these men and leave them alone, for if this plan or this work is of men, it will be overthrown;
but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them—lest you even be found fighting against God.” And they were persuaded by him,
and having called in the apostles, they beat them and commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
So they went out from the presence of the council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the name.
And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news that the Christ is Jesus.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 · The Seven Chosen; Stephen Arrested
chapters.intro: As the disciples grow in number, the Greek-speaking group complains that its widows are passed over in the daily distribution of food. The twelve have the community choose seven men to take charge of it, so that they themselves can keep to prayer and preaching; Stephen and Philip are among the seven. Stephen does many signs; men who cannot out-argue him put up false witnesses to say he speaks against the temple and the law, and he is brought before the council.

verses.en: Now in those days, as the disciples were increasing in number, there arose a complaint of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.

cmp.note: 原文是「希腊化的人」对「希伯来人」，两边都是信了耶稣的犹太人：一般认为前者是从外地回来、平常说希腊话的，后者是本地说亚兰话（或希伯来话）的。和合本译「说希利尼话的犹太人」「希伯来人」。
cmp.en: The Greek sets "Hellenists" against "Hebrews"; both are Jewish believers. The first are generally taken to be Jews from abroad whose everyday language was Greek, the second local Jews who spoke Aramaic (or Hebrew). The Union Version has 说希利尼话的犹太人 (shuō Xīlìní huà de Yóutàirén, "Jews who speak Greek") and 希伯来人 (Xībóláirén, "Hebrews").

verses.en: And the twelve summoned the whole body of the disciples and said, “It is not right that we should give up the word of God to serve tables.
Therefore, brothers, pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint over this duty;
but we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

And what was said pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch,
whom they set before the apostles, and having prayed they laid their hands on them.
And the word of God kept spreading, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem was multiplying greatly, and a great crowd of the priests were becoming obedient to the faith.
And Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
But some of those from the synagogue called that of the Freedmen, and of the Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen,
and they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he was speaking.
Then they secretly put up men to say, “We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and coming upon him they seized him and brought him to the council,
and they set up false witnesses who said, “This man does not cease speaking words against this holy place and the law,
for we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and will change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”
And gazing at him, all who were sitting in the council saw his face as the face of an angel.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 · Stephen’s Speech and Death
chapters.intro: The high priest asks Stephen whether the charges against him are true. From verse 2 to verse 53 Stephen alone is speaking: he goes through the story of Israel from Abraham to Joseph, Moses, the tent in the wilderness and Solomon’s temple, says that the ancestors kept refusing those whom God sent, and ends by accusing his hearers of doing the same. Enraged, they drag him out of the city and stone him to death.

verses.en: And the high priest said, “Are these things so?”
And he said, “Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran,
and said to him, ‘Go out from your land and from your kindred, and come into the land that I will show you.’

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《创世记》12:1。司提反这篇话从头到尾在讲旧约里的事，引文很多，出处写在各节的对照注里。
cmp.en: Quoted from Genesis 12:1. Stephen’s whole speech retells the Old Testament and quotes it often; the references are given in the notes under each verse.

verses.en: Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. And from there, after his father died, God moved him into this land in which you are now living,
and he gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot’s length, and he promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his offspring after him, though he had no child.
And God spoke in this way: that his offspring would be sojourners in a land belonging to others, and that they would enslave them and mistreat them four hundred years.

cmp.note: 这一节和下一节引的是《创世记》15:13–14。
cmp.en: This verse and the next quote Genesis 15:13–14.

verses.en: ‘And the nation that they serve as slaves I will judge,’ said God, ‘and after these things they will come out and worship me in this place.’
And he gave him a covenant of circumcision; and so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
And the patriarchs, jealous of Joseph, sold him into Egypt; and God was with him,
and rescued him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.
Now a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers could find no food.
But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers the first time.
And on the second visit Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph’s family became known to Pharaoh.
And Joseph sent and called for Jacob his father and all his kindred, seventy-five persons in all.

cmp.note: 旧约希伯来文本的《创世记》46:27 写的是七十人；这里的七十五，和旧约的古希腊文译本一致。
cmp.en: The Hebrew text of Genesis 46:27 has seventy; the seventy-five here agrees with the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament.

verses.en: And Jacob went down into Egypt. And he died, he and our fathers,
and they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.

cmp.note: 按旧约《创世记》，在示剑向哈抹的儿子们买地的是雅各（33:19），亚伯拉罕买的坟地在希伯仑（第 23 章）。这里照司提反的话译，没有改。
cmp.en: In Genesis it is Jacob who buys land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor (33:19), while the burial ground Abraham buys is at Hebron (chapter 23). The translation follows Stephen’s words as they stand.

verses.en: But as the time of the promise that God had declared to Abraham was drawing near, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt,
until another king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
He dealt craftily with our people and mistreated our fathers, making them expose their infants so that they would not be kept alive.
At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful before God; and he was brought up three months in his father’s house,
and when he was exposed, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up and brought him up as her own son.
And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds.
But when he was approaching the age of forty, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
And seeing one of them being wronged, he defended him and avenged the man who was being oppressed, striking down the Egyptian.
Now he supposed that his brothers would understand that God was giving them deliverance by his hand, but they did not understand.
And on the following day he appeared to them as they were fighting and tried to reconcile them to peace, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers; why do you wrong each other?’
But the man who was wronging his neighbor pushed him aside, saying, ‘Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?

cmp.note: 这一节和下一节引的是《出埃及记》2:14。第 35 节司提反再引一次这句话。
cmp.en: This verse and the next quote Exodus 2:14. Stephen repeats the question in verse 35.

verses.en: Do you want to kill me the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
And at this word Moses fled and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
And when forty years had passed, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.
And when Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight; and as he was drawing near to look, there came the voice of the Lord:
‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.’ And Moses trembled and did not dare to look.

cmp.w: Egō ho theos tōn paterōn sou
cmp.note: 第 32–34 节引的是《出埃及记》3:5–10，次序和那里略有不同。
cmp.en: Verses 32–34 quote Exodus 3:5–10, in a slightly different order.

verses.en: And the Lord said to him, ‘Take off the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.
I have surely seen the mistreatment of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. And now come, I will send you to Egypt.’
This Moses, whom they rejected, saying, ‘Who appointed you ruler and judge?’—this man God sent as both ruler and redeemer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
This man led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and at the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’

cmp.note: 引的是《申命记》18:15。
cmp.en: Quoted from Deuteronomy 18:15.

verses.en: This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai and with our fathers, who received living oracles to give to us,

cmp.note: 原文这个词本来是「聚集起来的一群人」，这里指旷野里的以色列会众；这卷书别处用同一个词指信耶稣的人聚成的群体，中文译「教会」。
cmp.en: The Greek word means "a gathered assembly"; here it is the congregation of Israel in the wilderness. Elsewhere in this book the same word is used for the community of those who believe in Jesus and is translated "church" (教会 jiàohuì in Chinese).

verses.en: to whom our fathers were unwilling to be obedient, but pushed him aside and in their hearts turned back to Egypt,
saying to Aaron, ‘Make for us gods who will go before us; for this Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’

cmp.note: 引的是《出埃及记》32:1。
cmp.en: Quoted from Exodus 32:1.

verses.en: And they made a calf in those days, and offered a sacrifice to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of their hands.

But God turned away and gave them over to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring me slain beasts and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, the images that you made to worship; and I will remove you beyond Babylon.’

cmp.note: 第 42–43 节引的是旧约《阿摩司书》5:25–27，照的是古希腊文译本。那里末句是「迁到大马色以外」，这里说的是「巴比伦的那一边」。
cmp.en: Verses 42–43 quote Amos 5:25–27 in the form of the ancient Greek translation. There the last line reads "beyond Damascus"; here it is "beyond Babylon."

verses.en: Our fathers had the tent of testimony in the wilderness, just as the one who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen.
Our fathers in turn received it and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the nations whom God drove out before our fathers, until the days of David,

cmp.note: 「约书亚」和「耶稣」在希腊文里是同一个名字。这里说的是旧约里接替摩西、带以色列人进迦南的约书亚。
cmp.en: "Joshua" and "Jesus" are the same name in Greek. The one meant here is the Joshua of the Old Testament, who succeeded Moses and led Israel into Canaan.

verses.en: who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
But it was Solomon who built a house for him.
Yet the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands, as the prophet says:
‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what is the place of my rest?

cmp.en: Verses 49–50 quote Isaiah 66:1–2.

verses.en: Did not my hand make all these things?’
You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.

cmp.note: 「硬着脖子」「心和耳朵没有受过割礼」都是旧约里责备以色列人的说法（如《出埃及记》33:3、《耶利米书》6:10），意思是不肯听、不肯顺服。
cmp.en: "Stiff-necked" and "uncircumcised in heart and ears" are Old Testament reproaches of Israel (for example Exodus 33:3; Jeremiah 6:10), meaning unwilling to listen or to yield.

verses.en: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced beforehand the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers,
you who received the law as delivered by angels, and did not keep it.”
Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they ground their teeth at him.
But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God,
and he said, “Look, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
But they cried out with a loud voice and stopped their ears and rushed together upon him,
and they threw him out of the city and began to stone him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man called Saul.
And they were stoning Stephen as he called out and said, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
And kneeling down he cried out with a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And having said this, he fell asleep.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 · Persecution; Philip in Samaria; the Ethiopian Eunuch
chapters.intro: After Stephen’s death a great persecution falls on the church in Jerusalem; the believers scatter and Saul goes about arresting them. Philip preaches in Samaria and many believe. Simon, a magician, offers money for the apostles’ power to give the Holy Spirit by laying on hands, and Peter rebukes him. Then, on a desert road, Philip explains a passage of Isaiah to an Ethiopian court official and baptizes him.

verses.en: And Saul was approving of his killing. And on that day a great persecution arose against the church in Jerusalem, and they were all scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
And devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him.
But Saul was ravaging the church; entering house after house, he dragged off both men and women and delivered them to prison.
Now those who were scattered went about proclaiming the good news of the word.
And Philip went down to the city of Samaria and was proclaiming the Christ to them.
And the crowds with one accord paid attention to what was being said by Philip, as they heard him and saw the signs that he was doing.
For unclean spirits, crying out with a loud voice, were coming out of many who had them, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
And there was much joy in that city.
But a man named Simon had previously been practicing magic in the city and amazing the people of Samaria, saying that he himself was someone great,
to whom they all paid attention, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is the power of God that is called Great.”
And they paid attention to him because for a long time he had amazed them with his magic.
But when they believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were being baptized, both men and women.
And even Simon himself believed, and after being baptized he stayed close to Philip; and seeing signs and great works of power taking place, he was amazed.
Now when the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent to them Peter and John,
who went down and prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit;
for it had not yet fallen on any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then they were laying their hands on them, and they were receiving the Holy Spirit.
Now when Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money,
saying, “Give me this authority also, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”
But Peter said to him, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought to obtain the gift of God with money!
You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
Repent therefore of this wickedness of yours, and pray to the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and the bond of unrighteousness.”
And Simon answered and said, “Pray for me to the Lord yourselves, that nothing of what you have said may come upon me.”
Now when they had solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they were returning to Jerusalem, and they were proclaiming the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.
Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Rise and go toward the south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.” This is a desert road.

cmp.note: 这个说法可以是「往南」，也可以是「在正午」；白话和英文都取「往南」，和合本也是。
cmp.en: The phrase can mean "toward the south" or "at noon." Both translations take it as "toward the south," as does the Union Version.

verses.en: And he rose and went. And there was an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a court official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship,

cmp.note: 一般认为「干大基」是那个国家对女王的称号，不是某一位女王的名字。
cmp.en: "Candace" is generally thought to have been the title of that kingdom’s queens rather than one queen’s personal name.

verses.en: and was returning and sitting in his chariot, and he was reading the prophet Isaiah.
And the Spirit said to Philip, “Go up and join this chariot.”
And Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
And he said, “How could I, unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
Now the passage of the scripture that he was reading was this: “Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.

cmp.note: 第 32–33 节引的是《以赛亚书》53:7–8，照的是古希腊文译本，和希伯来文本的字句有出入。
cmp.en: Verses 32–33 quote Isaiah 53:7–8 in the form of the ancient Greek translation, which differs in wording from the Hebrew text.

verses.en: In his humiliation his justice was taken away. Who will describe his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth.”
And the eunuch answered Philip and said, “I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this? About himself, or about someone else?”
And Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this scripture he proclaimed to him the good news of Jesus.
And as they were going along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch says, “Look, water! What prevents me from being baptized?”
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本这里有一段问答：腓利说，只要你全心相信，就可以受洗；那人回答说，他信耶稣基督是上帝的儿子。最早的几份抄本没有这一节，一般认为是后来加进来的，所以底本不收。节号照旧留着，后面各节的编号才不会变。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have an exchange here: Philip says that he may be baptized if he believes with all his heart, and the man answers that he believes Jesus Christ is the Son of God. The earliest manuscripts lack the verse, and it is generally thought to be a later addition, so the edition leaves it out. The verse number is kept so that the numbering of the following verses does not change.

verses.en: And he ordered the chariot to stop, and they both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he was going on his way rejoicing.
But Philip was found at Azotus, and as he passed through he was proclaiming the good news to all the towns until he came to Caesarea.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · Saul on the Road to Damascus; Peter at Lydda and Joppa
chapters.intro: Saul sets out for Damascus with letters from the high priest to arrest those who believe in Jesus. Near the city a light from heaven strikes him down, he hears Jesus speaking to him, and he is blind for three days. A disciple named Ananias is sent to lay hands on him; Saul recovers his sight, is baptized, and begins to proclaim Jesus, so that now he is the one hunted. The chapter ends with Peter healing a paralyzed man at Lydda and raising Tabitha at Joppa.

verses.en: But Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to Damascus, to the synagogues, so that if he found any who belonged to the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

cmp.note: 字面是「那条路」。这卷书几次用它称呼信耶稣的这一群人（另见 19:9、19:23、22:4、24:14、24:22），这里是第一次。和合本译「这道」。
cmp.en: Literally "the road." This book several times uses it as a name for the group who believe in Jesus (see also 19:9; 19:23; 22:4; 24:14; 24:22); this is the first. The Union Version has 这道 (zhè dào, "this way").

verses.en: Now as he was going, it happened that he was drawing near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him,
and falling to the ground he heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
And he said, “Who are you, Lord?” And he said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting;
but rise and enter the city, and it will be told you what you must do.”
Now the men who were traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.
And Saul rose from the ground, and though his eyes were opened he saw nothing; and leading him by the hand they brought him into Damascus.
And for three days he was without sight, and neither ate nor drank.
Now there was a disciple at Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias.” And he said, “Here I am, Lord.”
And the Lord said to him, “Rise and go to the street called Straight, and look in the house of Judas for a man of Tarsus named Saul; for look, he is praying,
and he has seen in a vision a man named Ananias come in and lay his hands on him so that he might see again.”
But Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much harm he has done to your saints in Jerusalem;
and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on your name.”
But the Lord said to him, “Go, for this man is a chosen instrument of mine to carry my name before nations and kings and the sons of Israel;
for I will show him how much he must suffer for the sake of my name.”

And Ananias departed and entered the house, and laying his hands on him he said, “Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me, Jesus who appeared to you on the road by which you came, so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he saw again; and he rose and was baptized,
and taking food he was strengthened. And he was with the disciples at Damascus for some days,
and immediately in the synagogues he was proclaiming Jesus, that he is the Son of God.

And all who heard were amazed and were saying, “Is this not the man who in Jerusalem made havoc of those who call on this name? And had he not come here for this purpose, to bring them bound before the chief priests?”
But Saul was growing all the more in strength, and was confounding the Jews who lived in Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
Now when many days had passed, the Jews plotted to kill him,
but their plot became known to Saul. And they were even watching the gates day and night in order to kill him;
but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
And when he had come to Jerusalem, he was attempting to join the disciples; and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and described to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
And he was with them, going in and out at Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord,
and he was speaking and disputing with the Hellenists; but they were attempting to kill him.
And when the brothers learned of it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
So the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up; and walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it was multiplied.

cmp.note: 本站的底本这里「教会」是单数，把三个地区的信徒当成一个整体；多数较晚的抄本是复数「各教会」，和合本的「各处的教会」跟的是后者。
cmp.en: In the edition this site follows "the church" is singular here, treating the believers of all three regions as one body; most later manuscripts have the plural "churches," which the Union Version follows with 各处的教会 (gè chù de jiàohuì, "the churches in every place").

verses.en: Now it happened that as Peter was passing through all those parts, he came down also to the saints who lived at Lydda.
And there he found a man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a mat for eight years, who was paralyzed.
And Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you; rise and make your bed.” And immediately he rose.
And all who lived at Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
Now in Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas; she was full of good works and acts of charity that she was doing.

cmp.note: 「大比大」是亚兰话，「多加」是希腊话，两个词都是「羚羊」的意思。「翻出来就是多加」是经文原有的话，所以没有放进圆括号。
cmp.en: "Tabitha" is Aramaic and "Dorcas" is Greek; both mean "gazelle." The words "which translated means Dorcas" belong to the text itself, so the Chinese does not put them in parentheses.

verses.en: And it happened in those days that she fell sick and died; and having washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
Now since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging him, “Do not delay in coming to us.”

And Peter rose and went with them. And when he arrived, they brought him up into the upper room, and all the widows stood beside him weeping and showing the tunics and garments that Dorcas used to make while she was with them.
But Peter put them all outside, and kneeling down he prayed; and turning to the body he said, “Tabitha, rise.” And she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter she sat up.
And giving her his hand he raised her up; and calling the saints and the widows, he presented her alive.
And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
And it happened that he stayed many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · Cornelius and Peter
chapters.intro: Cornelius, a Roman officer, is not a Jew but worships God. An angel tells him to send to Joppa for Peter. Peter meanwhile sees in a vision a great sheet full of animals that Jews are forbidden to eat, and hears a voice say that what God has made clean must not be called common. He goes to Cornelius’s house and tells the story of Jesus; before he has finished, the Holy Spirit falls on these non-Jews, and he has them baptized.

verses.en: Now there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of what was called the Italian Cohort,
a devout man who feared God with all his household, who gave many alms to the people and prayed to God continually.

cmp.note: 字面是「敬畏上帝的」。这卷书用这个说法称呼那些不是犹太人、却敬拜犹太人的上帝的人（另见 13:16、13:26）。
cmp.en: Literally "one who fears God." This book uses the phrase for people who were not Jews but worshiped the God of the Jews (see also 13:16; 13:26).

verses.en: About the ninth hour of the day he saw clearly in a vision an angel of God coming in to him and saying to him, “Cornelius.”
And he stared at him and, becoming afraid, said, “What is it, Lord?” And he said to him, “Your prayers and your alms have gone up as a memorial before God.
And now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter;
he is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea.”
And when the angel who was speaking to him had departed, he called two of his household servants and a devout soldier from among those who attended him,
and having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.
Now on the next day, as they were on their journey and approaching the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour.
And he became hungry and wanted to eat; but while they were preparing it, a trance came upon him,
and he sees the heaven opened and a certain object coming down, like a great sheet, being let down by its four corners upon the earth,
in which were all the four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth and birds of the heaven.
And there came a voice to him: “Rise, Peter; kill and eat.”
But Peter said, “By no means, Lord; for I have never eaten anything common and unclean.”

cmp.note: 犹太律法把动物分成可以吃的和不可以吃的（旧约《利未记》第 11 章），不可以吃的叫「不洁净」。「俗的」原文是「普通的、大家共用的」，在这里指没有照律法分别出来的。
cmp.en: Jewish law divides animals into those that may be eaten and those that may not (Leviticus 11); the forbidden ones are called "unclean." "Common" here means not set apart as the law requires.

verses.en: And a voice came to him again a second time: “What God has made clean, do not you call common.”
This happened three times, and immediately the object was taken up into heaven.

Now while Peter was greatly perplexed in himself as to what the vision that he had seen might be, look, the men who had been sent by Cornelius, having asked their way to Simon’s house, stood at the gate,
and calling out they were asking whether Simon who is called Peter was lodging there.
And while Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Look, men are looking for you;
but rise, go down, and go with them without hesitation, for I have sent them.”
And Peter went down to the men and said, “Look, I am the one you are looking for; what is the reason for which you have come?”

And they said, “Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous and God-fearing man, well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, was directed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear words from you.”
So he invited them in and lodged them. And on the next day he rose and went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went with him.
And on the following day he entered Caesarea. And Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
And when it came about that Peter entered, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet and worshiped.
But Peter raised him up, saying, “Stand up; I myself also am a man.”
And talking with him he went in, and he finds many gathered together,
and he said to them, “You yourselves know how unlawful it is for a Jewish man to associate with or to visit a foreigner; and yet God has shown me that I should call no person common or unclean.
Therefore I came without even raising an objection when I was sent for. I ask, then, for what reason you sent for me.”
And Cornelius said, “Four days ago, to this very hour, I was praying in my house at the ninth hour, and look, a man stood before me in bright clothing
and says, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard and your alms have been remembered before God.
Send therefore to Joppa and call for Simon who is called Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon, a tanner, by the sea.’
So I sent to you at once, and you have done well to come. Now therefore we are all here present before God to hear all that has been commanded you by the Lord.”
And Peter opened his mouth and said, “In truth I understand that God shows no partiality,
but in every nation the one who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
As for the word that he sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ—he is Lord of all—
you yourselves know the thing that took place throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed:
Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
And we are witnesses of all that he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; whom they also killed by hanging him on a tree.

cmp.note: 「挂在木头上」指钉十字架；这个说法来自旧约《申命记》21:22–23，那里说被挂在木头上的人是受咒诅的。
cmp.en: "Hanging on a tree" means crucifixion; the wording comes from Deuteronomy 21:22–23, which says that one who is hanged on a tree is under a curse.

verses.en: This man God raised on the third day and granted that he should become visible,
not to all the people but to witnesses who had been chosen beforehand by God, to us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
And he commanded us to proclaim to the people and to testify solemnly that this is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead.
To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all who were hearing the word.
And the believers from among the circumcised, as many as had come with Peter, were amazed, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the nations also;
for they were hearing them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered,
“Can anyone withhold the water, so that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we also did?”
And he ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay on for some days.

chapters.title: Chapter 11 · Peter Explains in Jerusalem; the Church at Antioch
chapters.intro: In Jerusalem the circumcised believers challenge Peter for entering the house of non-Jews and eating with them. Peter tells them, step by step, about his vision at Joppa and what happened in Cornelius’s house, and they raise no further objection. Meanwhile those who had been scattered carry the word as far as Antioch; Barnabas goes there and then fetches Saul, and it is in Antioch that the believers are first called Christians.

verses.en: Now the apostles and the brothers who were throughout Judea heard that the nations also had received the word of God.
And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those from among the circumcised were disputing with him,
saying, “You went in to men who are uncircumcised and ate with them.”
But Peter began and explained it to them in order, saying,
“I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision, a certain object coming down, like a great sheet, being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right to me.
Staring at it, I was observing, and I saw the four-footed animals of the earth and the wild beasts and the reptiles and the birds of the heaven.
And I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Rise, Peter; kill and eat.’
But I said, ‘By no means, Lord; for nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
But a voice answered a second time from heaven, ‘What God has made clean, do not you call common.’
This happened three times, and everything was drawn up again into heaven.
And look, at that very moment three men stood at the house in which we were, having been sent to me from Caesarea.
And the Spirit told me to go with them without hesitation. And these six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s house.
And he reported to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter,
who will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and all your household.’
And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them just as on us at the beginning.
And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he used to say, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’

cmp.note: 这句话见这卷书的 1:5，是耶稣复活以后对使徒说的。
cmp.en: The saying is found at 1:5 of this book, spoken by Jesus to the apostles after his resurrection.

verses.en: If then God gave to them the same gift as he gave also to us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I could hinder God?”
And when they heard these things they fell silent, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, to the nations also God has granted the repentance that leads to life.”
Now those who were scattered because of the affliction that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews only.
But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who on coming to Antioch were speaking to the Hellenists also, proclaiming the good news of the Lord Jesus.

cmp.note: 本站的底本这里是「说希腊话的人」（和 9:29 同一个词）；另一些抄本是「希腊人」，和合本的「希利尼人」跟的是后者。上一节说只对犹太人讲，这一节说「也」对这些人讲，所以一般认为这里指的是不是犹太人的人。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "Hellenists," speakers of Greek (the same word as in 9:29); other manuscripts read "Greeks," which the Union Version follows with 希利尼人 (Xīlìní rén, "Greeks"). Since the previous verse says they spoke only to Jews and this verse says "also," the people meant here are generally taken to be non-Jews.

verses.en: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number who believed turned to the Lord.
And the report about them came to the ears of the church that was in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas out as far as Antioch;
who, when he arrived and saw the grace of God, rejoiced, and he was exhorting them all to remain with the Lord with purpose of heart,
for he was a good man and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.
And he went out to Tarsus to look for Saul,

and when he had found him he brought him to Antioch. And it came about that for a whole year they were gathered together with the church and taught a considerable crowd; and it was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
Now in these days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
And one of them named Agabus stood up and indicated through the Spirit that there was going to be a great famine over the whole inhabited world; this took place in the time of Claudius.
And the disciples, each according to his means, determined to send relief to the brothers living in Judea;
and this they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 · James Killed, Peter Freed, Herod’s Death
chapters.intro: King Herod has the apostle James killed and puts Peter in prison, meaning to deal with him after the Passover. In the night an angel leads Peter out; he goes to the house of Mark’s mother, where the people praying for him at first refuse to believe it is he. Later, in Caesarea, Herod accepts the crowd’s flattery, does not give the glory to God, and dies eaten by worms. At the end Barnabas and Saul finish their errand and go back, taking Mark with them.

verses.en: Now about that time Herod the king laid hands on some of those from the church, to do them harm.

cmp.note: 这位希律王是亚基帕一世，福音书里杀施洗约翰的那个希律的侄子，公元 41 到 44 年管犹太全地。
cmp.en: This King Herod is Agrippa I, nephew of the Herod who had John the Baptist killed in the Gospels; he ruled all Judea from 41 to 44 CE.

verses.en: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
And seeing that it pleased the Jews, he went on to arrest Peter also—those were the days of Unleavened Bread—
and having seized him, he put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending after the Passover to bring him out to the people.
So Peter was kept in the prison, but prayer for him was being made earnestly to God by the church.
Now when Herod was about to bring him out, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping watch over the prison.
And look, an angel of the Lord stood by, and a light shone in the cell; and striking Peter’s side he woke him, saying, “Get up quickly.” And his chains fell off his hands.
And the angel said to him, “Fasten your belt and put on your sandals.” And he did so. And he says to him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”
And going out he followed, and he did not know that what was being done through the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision.

And passing the first guard and the second, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened for them of its own accord; and going out they went along one street, and immediately the angel left him.
And Peter, coming to himself, said, “Now I truly know that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all that the people of the Jews were expecting.”
And when he realized this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.
And when he knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
And recognizing Peter’s voice, in her joy she did not open the gate, but ran in and reported that Peter was standing before the gate.
And they said to her, “You are out of your mind.” But she kept insisting that it was so. And they were saying, “It is his angel.”
But Peter continued knocking; and when they opened, they saw him and were astonished.

But motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he described to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison, and he said, “Report these things to James and to the brothers.” And going out he went to another place.

cmp.note: 第 2 节的雅各已经被杀，这里是另一位雅各。一般认为他是耶稣的兄弟，后来在耶路撒冷的教会里带头，第 15 章的会议上作结论的就是他。
cmp.en: The James of verse 2 has been killed; this is another James. He is generally taken to be the brother of Jesus, later the leading figure in the church at Jerusalem, who sums up at the council in chapter 15.

verses.en: Now when day came, there was no small disturbance among the soldiers over what had become of Peter.
And Herod, after searching for him and not finding him, examined the guards and ordered that they be led away. And going down from Judea to Caesarea, he stayed there.

Now he was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon; and with one accord they came to him, and having won over Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their country was fed from the king’s country.
And on an appointed day Herod, having put on royal clothing and taken his seat on the platform, was delivering a speech to them.
And the crowd was shouting, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”
And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give the glory to God; and he was eaten by worms and breathed his last.
But the word of God grew and multiplied.
And Barnabas and Saul returned, having completed their service in Jerusalem, taking along with them John who was called Mark.

cmp.note: 这一节的原文很难：字面像是「回到耶路撒冷」，可是上一章末说他们正是被派去耶路撒冷的；有的抄本作「从耶路撒冷」。底本加了一个逗号，把「耶路撒冷」连到「办完差事」上读，本站照底本；和合本作「从耶路撒冷回来」。
cmp.en: The Greek here is difficult: it seems to say "returned to Jerusalem," yet the end of the previous chapter has them sent to Jerusalem; some manuscripts read "from Jerusalem." This site’s edition adds a comma so that "Jerusalem" goes with "having completed their service," and the translation follows it; the Union Version has 从耶路撒冷回来 (cóng Yēlùsālěng huílái, "came back from Jerusalem").

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · Barnabas and Paul Sent Out: Cyprus and Pisidian Antioch
chapters.intro: At the Holy Spirit’s direction the church in Antioch sends Barnabas and Saul out. On Cyprus a magician tries to keep the proconsul from listening; Saul, from here on called Paul, rebukes him and he goes blind. At Antioch in Pisidia Paul gives a long speech in the synagogue, from the history of Israel to the raising of Jesus. When the Jews oppose them, the two turn to the Gentiles. Verses 16 to 41 are all Paul speaking.

verses.en: Now there were in Antioch, in the church that was there, prophets and teachers: Barnabas, and Simeon who was called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

cmp.note: 这是福音书里管加利利的那个希律，不是上一章死去的希律王。「分封王」是罗马之下只管一小块地方的统治者。
cmp.en: This is the Herod who ruled Galilee in the Gospels, not the King Herod who died in the previous chapter. A "tetrarch" was a ruler of a small territory under Rome.

verses.en: And while they were serving the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”
Then, having fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them off.
So they, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus;
and when they were in Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; and they also had John as their helper.
And when they had gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain man, a magician, a Jewish false prophet, whose name was Bar-Jesus,
who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. He summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the magician—for so his name is translated—was opposing them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
But Saul, who is also Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him

cmp.note: 扫罗是他的希伯来名字，保罗是他的罗马名字，是同一个人的两个名字。这卷书从这里起一直叫他保罗；原文并没有说他在这时改了名。
cmp.en: Saul is his Hebrew name and Paul his Roman name: two names for one man. From here on the book calls him Paul; the text does not say that he changed his name at this point.

verses.en: and said, “O you who are full of all deceit and all villainy, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop making crooked the straight ways of the Lord?

And now, look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.” And immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and going about he was seeking people to lead him by the hand.
Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
Now Paul and those with him put out to sea from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia; but John left them and returned to Jerusalem.
But they, passing on from Perga, arrived at Pisidian Antioch, and going into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down.
And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, “Men, brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, say it.”
And Paul stood up, and motioning with his hand said: “Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.
The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and he made the people great during their stay in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm he led them out of it;
and for about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness;

cmp.note: 底本是「容忍他们」；另有抄本只差一个字母（etrophophorēsen），意思是「像父亲一样抚养他们」。和合本与底本一致。
cmp.en: This site’s edition reads "put up with them"; other manuscripts differ by one letter (etrophophorēsen), meaning "cared for them as a father." The Union Version agrees with the edition.

verses.en: and having destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land as an inheritance—
all this took about four hundred and fifty years. And after these things he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

cmp.note: 底本把「约四百五十年」连在前面，指从寄居埃及到分得土地这一段；和合本连在后面，说士师的时代约有四百五十年，那是较晚抄本的语序。
cmp.en: This site’s edition attaches "about four hundred and fifty years" to what precedes, the span from the stay in Egypt to the gift of the land. The Union Version attaches it to what follows, making the period of the judges about 450 years; that follows the word order of later manuscripts.

verses.en: And then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
And having removed him, he raised up David to be their king, of whom he also testified and said, ‘I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who will do all my will.’

cmp.note: 这句话合了旧约的几处：《诗篇》89:20 和《撒母耳记上》13:14。
cmp.en: The saying combines several Old Testament passages: Psalm 89:20 and 1 Samuel 13:14.

verses.en: From this man’s offspring God, according to promise, brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus,
after John had proclaimed beforehand, before his coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
And as John was finishing his course, he was saying, ‘What do you suppose that I am? I am not he. But look, one is coming after me, the sandal of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’
Men, brothers, sons of the family of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to us the word of this salvation has been sent out.
For those who live in Jerusalem and their rulers, not recognizing this one nor the voices of the prophets that are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him;
and though they found no cause for death, they asked Pilate that he be put to death.
And when they had carried out all that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead;
and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses to the people.
And we bring you the good news of the promise made to the fathers,
that God has fulfilled this to our children by raising Jesus, as also it is written in the second psalm, ‘You are my Son; today I have begotten you.’

cmp.note: 底本是「向我们的儿女」，这是最早几份抄本的读法，读起来有些别扭；较晚的抄本作「向他们的儿女，就是我们」，和合本的「向我们这作儿女的」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: This site’s edition reads "to our children," the reading of the earliest manuscripts, awkward as it is. Later manuscripts read "to their children, to us," which the Union Version follows with 向我们这作儿女的 (xiàng wǒmen zhè zuò érnǚ de, "to us who are the children").

verses.en: And as for the fact that he raised him from the dead, no more to return to decay, he has spoken in this way: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’

cmp.note: 引自《以赛亚书》55:3，照的是希腊文旧约的字句。
cmp.en: Quoted from Isaiah 55:3, in the wording of the Greek Old Testament.

verses.en: Therefore he also says in another psalm, ‘You will not let your Holy One see decay.’

cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 16:10.

verses.en: For David, after he had served the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep and was laid with his fathers and saw decay;
but he whom God raised did not see decay.
Let it be known to you therefore, men, brothers, that through this one forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and from all the things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses,
in this one everyone who believes is justified.
See to it, then, that what is said in the prophets does not come upon you:
‘Look, you scoffers, and be amazed and perish; for I am doing a work in your days, a work that you will certainly not believe, even if someone tells it to you.’”

cmp.note: 引自《哈巴谷书》1:5，照的是希腊文旧约的字句。
cmp.en: Quoted from Habakkuk 1:5, in the wording of the Greek Old Testament.

verses.en: And as they were going out, the people were begging that these things be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.
And when the synagogue had broken up, many of the Jews and of the devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking to them, were urging them to continue in the grace of God.
And on the coming Sabbath almost the whole city was gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and were contradicting what was spoken by Paul, reviling him.

And Paul and Barnabas, speaking boldly, said, “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken first to you. Since you thrust it aside and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.
For so the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you may be for salvation to the end of the earth.’”

cmp.note: 引自《以赛亚书》49:6。
cmp.en: Quoted from Isaiah 49:6.

verses.en: And when the Gentiles heard this, they were rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
And the word of the Lord was spreading through the whole region.
